subject: Re: Starlane pilot - load playbook & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@starlane.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@starlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Starlane kickoff - traffic snapshot and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick summary and the payload sample I promised.

Quick facts from our side:
- Primary product: Starlane Search Assist (user queries -> multi-turn clarifying + code/gen snippets).
- Typical query length: 40–180 tokens; 95th pct response length ~520 tokens (including system + assistant).
- Baseline steady-state: ~4–6 RPS (global), concurrency typically 10–15 active sessions.
- Peak bursts during marketing events: short spikes up to ~220 RPS for ~3–7 minutes (we saw this last quarter).
- Token mix: average request tokens ~30, average response tokens ~320.

Attached: starlane_sample_payloads.json (JSON) — includes representative prompts and multi-turn traces.

As discussed, our goals for a pilot: verify latency & cost assumptions for the 512-token response case, confirm reliability during short bursts, and validate that your runtime can preserve session KV cache across our multi-turn flows.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm the minimum footprint/config you recommend for the pilot to represent our 6 RPS baseline and 220 RPS burst?
2) What telemetry and tagging do you need us to include in the payloads to map requests to sessions and user tiers?
3) Proposed timeline — we'd like a 3-week pilot window starting next Monday if that works for you.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up if any of the above needs clarifying.

— Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform
Starlane AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@starlane.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Starlane kickoff - traffic snapshot and next steps

Elena — thanks, this is exactly what we needed. Recap and proposed pilot playbook below.

Recap of the workload fingerprint you shared:
- Steady: 4–6 RPS, concurrency 10–15.
- Burst: up to ~220 RPS for short windows (3–7m).
- Response lengths: median ~320 tokens, 95th ~520 tokens.
- Multi-turn session behavior: KV cache/reuse important to preserve cost & latency.

Proposed pilot playbook (3-week window) — high level:
Week 0 (pre-checks, 2 business days): staging access + corpus ingestion; confirm tagging fields (session_id, user_tier, request_ts).
Week 1 (baseline verification, 5 business days): run steady-state tests, measure p50/p95 latency for 256/512 token responses, collect error logs and model trace sampling.
Week 2 (burst resilience & tuning, 5 business days): run synthetic bursts modeled on your sample (220 RPS for 5m windows), validate autoscaling policy and prefix/KV caching behavior.
Week 3 (cost & ops handoff, 3 business days): quantify per-token unit economics, recommend quantization/batching settings; final sign-off with your engineering + procurement.

Success criteria (draft — open for your edits):
- Latency: p95 <= 450ms for 512-token assistant responses under steady-state (6 RPS) and p95 <= 900ms during burst windows (220 RPS) with <=1% 5xx errors.
- Reliability: no sustained queueing/backpressure leading to request drops; autoscale triggers to keep error rate <1%.
- Functional: KV cache correctly reused across multi-turn sessions (we'll validate by trace sampling).
- Cost signal: projected token spend within 10% of your expectations after batching/quantization recommendations.

Technical asks from us to you:
- Provide a staging API key and a short-lived user that mirrors production auth so we can exercise the same paths.
- Confirm the region preference (us-west preferred for latency).
- Share any rate-limiting or downstream timeouts we should honor.

Neha — can you confirm an initial config (GPU class + concurrency target) and an ops contact for runbook handoff? Monica — can you flag any procurement constraints we should be aware of before Week 3?

If that looks good, we'll lock calendar blocks and drop the traffic matrix (CSV) with the exact inject schedule.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@starlane.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Starlane kickoff - traffic snapshot and next steps

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. Two clarifications and one scheduling tweak: 
1) Bursts: those 220 RPS spikes are global aggregated; region routing will send ~65–75% to us-west.
2) Session IDs: we'll add session_id + conversation_turn to the payloads; we'll push an updated sample by EOD.
3) Timeline: procurement needs a week to approve test keys. Can we shift start to next Monday two weeks out (so pilot window becomes Apr 5–25)?

Attached: starlane_poc_mvp.docx (MVP objectives and procurement points).

We'll also grant a staging service account with read/write keys (expiry 30 days). Ops contact is ops@starlane.ai — they'll coordinate firewall/IP allowlisting.

Elena

Subject: Re: Starlane pilot - shifted dates and intake confirmation

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications. Updated plan below with owners and the intake matrix attached.

Updated schedule: Pilot window Apr 5–25 (3 weeks testing + 1 week ramp/handoff).
Owners and immediate deliverables:
- Marcus Lin (Solutions): pilot orchestration, latency and error telemetry, final ops handoff.
- Neha Kapoor (SRE): staging cluster config, autoscale policy, and load injection schedule.
- Monica Patel (Customer Success): runbook acceptance, weekly syncs with Starlane eng.
- Starlane ops (ops@starlane.ai): grant staging keys, IP allowlist, provide updated payloads.

Workload intake fields we will use (please copy into your sample payloads):
- session_id (string)
- conversation_turn (int)
- user_tier (enum: free, pro, enterprise)
- request_tokens (int)
- response_tokens_est (int)
- arrival_rate_rps (float)
- region_hint (string)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)

Initial traffic matrix (attached): csv with stepwise inject schedule modeling baseline + two burst windows per day (5m at 220 RPS).
Acceptance criteria (final) will mirror the draft; we will run a joint sign-off meeting within 72 hours of the final test.

Attachments: starlane_traffic_matrix.csv (CSV) — contains the inject schedule / concurrency targets.

I'll queue the calendar invites for Apr 5 kickoff and a preflight on Apr 2 to confirm allowlisting and keys.

— Marcus
